title: Write a Word to a File and Read it Back
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read one word with `scanf`. Write it to a file named `data.txt` using `fprintf`, close the file, open it again for reading and read the word with `fscanf`.

Input: one word.
Output: `Read: ` followed by the word read from the file.
constraints: The word has at most 50 characters and no spaces

title: Save an Integer and Read it Back
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read an integer, write it to `number.txt` with `fprintf`, then read it back from the file with `fscanf` and print its double.

Input: one integer.
Output: a single integer, twice the value read from the file.

title: Copy a Word Character by Character
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read a word. Write it to `chars.txt` one character at a time with `fputc`. Then read the file back one character at a time with `fgetc` (until `EOF`) and print each character on its own line.

Input: one word.
Output: each character of the word on its own line.
constraints: The word has 1 to 20 characters and no spaces

title: Store a Sentence in a File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read one whole line with `fgets`. Write it to `line.txt` with `fputs`, then read the file back with `fgets` and print the line.

Input: one line of text (may contain spaces).
Output: the same line, read back from the file.
constraints: The line has at most 100 characters

title: Does the File Exist?
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read an integer `flag`. If `flag` is 1, create a file `exists.txt` containing the text `ok`. Then try to open `exists.txt` for reading with `fopen`. If `fopen` returns `NULL`, print `Not found`, otherwise print `Found` (and close the file).

Input: one integer, 0 or 1.
Output: `Found` or `Not found`.

title: Sum Numbers Stored in a File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n`, then `n` integers. Write them to `numbers.txt`, one per line. Reopen the file, read the numbers back with `fscanf` in a loop (until it no longer returns 1) and print their sum.

Input: `n` then `n` integers.
Output: the sum.

title: Append a Second Word
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read two words. Write the first to `log.txt` (mode `"w"`) followed by a newline. Then reopen `log.txt` in append mode (`"a"`) and add the second word and a newline. Finally read the file back and print its lines.

Input: two words separated by whitespace.
Output: the first word on line 1, the second on line 2.
constraints: Each word has at most 30 characters

title: Count Characters in a File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read one word and write it to `count.txt`. Reopen the file and count the characters using `fgetc` until `EOF`. Print the count.

Input: one word.
Output: the number of characters in the file.
constraints: The word has 1 to 50 characters and no spaces

title: Binary File of Integers
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n` and then `n` integers. Write the whole array to a binary file `nums.bin` with one `fwrite` call. Read it back into a second array with `fread` and print the values separated by single spaces.

Input: `n` then `n` integers.
Output: the integers on one line, separated by single spaces.

title: Largest Number in a File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n` and `n` integers. Write them to `values.txt` separated by spaces. Read the file back and print the largest number.

Input: `n` then `n` integers.
Output: the maximum value.

title: Lines, Words and Characters of a File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n`, then `n` lines of text (use `fgets`). Write the lines to `text.txt`, then read it back with `fgetc` and count lines (newline characters), words (groups of non-space characters) and characters (including newlines).

Input: `n`, then `n` lines.
Output: `lines words chars` separated by single spaces.
constraints: Each line has at most 80 characters and at least one word

a

title: Copy a File in Uppercase
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read a single line with `fgets` and write it to `source.txt`. Then copy `source.txt` to `copy.txt` character by character, converting letters to uppercase with `toupper`. Print the contents of `copy.txt`.

Input: one line of text.
Output: the line in uppercase.
constraints: The line has at most 100 characters

title: Merge Two Sorted Files
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n` then `n` sorted integers and write them to `a.txt`. Read `m` then `m` sorted integers and write them to `b.txt`. Merge the two files into `merged.txt` so the result stays sorted (compare the current numbers of both files). Print the contents of `merged.txt` on one line, separated by single spaces.

Input: `n`, `n` integers, `m`, `m` integers (both ascending).
Output: all numbers in ascending order.
constraints: Each list is in non-decreasing order

title: Count Vowels in a File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read one line of text with `fgets` and save it to `vowels.txt`. Read the file back with `fgetc` and count vowels (`a e i o u`, upper or lower case) and consonants (other letters). Ignore everything else.

Input: one line.
Output: `vowels consonants` separated by a single space.
constraints: The line has at most 100 characters

title: Top Student from a Record File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n`, then `n` students, each as a name (one word) and an integer mark. Store each as a `struct` and write all of them to the binary file `students.bin` using `fwrite`. Read the records back with `fread` and print the name and mark of the student with the highest mark (marks are all different).

Input: `n`, then `n` pairs `name mark`.
Output: `name mark`.

title: Jump to the k-th Number with fseek
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n` and `n` integers and write them to the binary file `data.bin` with `fwrite`. Then read `k` (1-based). Use `fseek` with `(k - 1) * sizeof(int)` from `SEEK_SET` to jump straight to the k-th integer and read it with `fread`. Print it.

Input: `n`, `n` integers, then `k`.
Output: the k-th integer.

title: Split Numbers into Even and Odd Files
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n` and `n` integers and write them to `all.txt`. Read `all.txt` back and write even numbers to `even.txt` and odd numbers to `odd.txt` (one per line). Finally print the contents of `even.txt` on one line, then `odd.txt` on the next line, numbers separated by single spaces. If a file is empty print an empty line.

Input: `n` then `n` non-negative integers.
Output: two lines (evens, then odds).

title: Print the Lines of a File in Reverse Order
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n`, then `n` lines of text (use `fgets`). Write the lines to `lines.txt`. Read the file back line by line into an array, then print the lines from last to first.

Input: `n`, then `n` lines.
Output: the lines in reverse order, one per line.

title: Word Frequency from a File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. Read `n` and then `n` words. Write them to `words.txt`, separated by spaces. Read the file back and count how many times each distinct word occurs (case-sensitive). Print each distinct word with its count, in order of first appearance, one `word count` pair per line.

Input: `n` then `n` words.
Output: lines of the form `word count`.
constraints: Each word has at most 20 characters

6
Apple apple Apple b b c

title: Update Records in a Binary File
description:
The judge starts with an empty folder, so your program must first CREATE the file itself and then read it back. A bank keeps accounts numbered 1 to `n` in the binary file `accounts.bin`; record `i` is one `int` balance. Read `n` and the `n` starting balances and write them with `fwrite`. Then read `q` operations, each `id amount` (amount may be negative). For each operation open the file in `"r+b"` mode, `fseek` to record `id`, `fread` the balance, add the amount, `fseek` back and `fwrite` the new balance. At the end read the whole file and print all balances separated by single spaces.

Input: `n`, `n` balances, `q`, then `q` pairs `id amount`.
Output: the final balances on one line.
